page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-240GB-1xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor with 12 vCPUs and 12 physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the processor includes advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 240.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPU with 80 GB of VRAM. This server does not include local storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities in specific single-threaded operations and machine learning tasks. The server achieves top-tier results in single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 15.51 GB/sec and Geekbench text processing at 2943.0. For language model workloads, the hardware delivers top-tier performance on small models, processing 10515.12 tokens per second for prompts and generating 547.27 tokens per second. General multi-core compute and memory bandwidth benchmarks, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 13282.0 and a large-block read memory bandwidth of 167.89 GB/sec, fall within the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce performance variability under sustained CPU-bound workloads, alongside the complete absence of local storage. However, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio and the presence of the NVIDIA H100 GPU make it highly efficient for memory-intensive machine learning, LLM inference, and data processing tasks. It is best suited for artificial intelligence workloads, deep learning model execution, and memory-heavy parallel computing tasks that do not require persistent local disk storage.
